title: 晩春の空が、青く澄み渡っている。 吹く風も心地よく、風に乗って聞こえてくる子供たちのはしゃぐ声は、始まったばかりの大型連

The late spring sky was clear and blue.  
The breeze was pleasant, and carried the sounds of children laughing and playing, as if already celebrating the start of the long holiday.
Unlike me, who was wasting time alone sitting on a park bench on the first day of the precious Golden Week for students.
They had no worries, no anxieties about the future—just innocent joy playing with their friends. Honestly, I was genuinely envious.
“I used to be like that too… or maybe I was a bit more twisted back then…? Well, whatever.”
Muttering something half-heartedly to myself, I looked up at the sky again.
Even though the blue sky stretched out without a single cloud, my mood was a completely different kind of blue. You could call it melancholy.
This was supposed to be the long-awaited Golden Week, but my current mood was overwhelmingly ennui.
Maybe that’s why a sigh mixed with regret slipped out.
“Man, I really messed up…”

Ever since Ijuuin transferred here, a bunch of things had been happening around me, but it was all worth it if I could somehow seal a contract to be supported for life by the zaibatsu heiress. That part was good.
But then, everything got muddled when Ijuuin got slapped down by Setsuna.

Thankfully, Ijuuin didn’t suffer any injuries after that, but maybe from hitting her head, during class she kept staring at Setsuna with an even more dreamy look than usual, ignoring what I was saying. Because of that, the plan for Ijuuin to support me financially quickly fell apart.
It was supposed to be a turning point in my life, a way to increase my income, but man, I was just unlucky. No wonder I sighed.
But well, that’s fine. It was never a definite contract anyway, so I can accept it.
The biggest problem now was that Setsuna and Arisa were trying to confine me.
I already knew Setsuna was a full-on yandere with extreme possessiveness, but Arisa switching from tsundere to yandere was completely unexpected.

Having those two childhood friends glare at me with eyes devoid of any highlights was traumatic. When they flanked me and dragged me out of the classroom into the hallway, I seriously feared for my safety.
If I hadn’t shouted loudly and some students from other classes hadn’t come to check on the commotion, I shudder to think what might have happened.
Afterwards, I managed to stop them from confining me by bowing down and coaxing them, but in exchange, I was forced to make a certain promise.
That promise was outrageous: during summer vacation, the two of them would stay at my house the entire time.

Even though they were idols and my childhood friends, two girls staying over at a guy’s house was a huge problem. Plus, my parents weren’t home, so it was basically no different from being confined under their watch.
I hoped their parents wouldn’t approve, but to my despair, both of them gave permission without hesitation. Words cannot describe how hopeless that felt.
“What do you mean, ‘Please take care of our Setsuna♪ Thanks, future husband♪’?”

Arisa’s parents said, “We entrust our daughter to you. Well, since she’ll be supporting you, maybe we’re the ones being entrusted? Anyway, we’re looking forward to seeing our grandchild’s face! Oh, can I call myself Grandpa?” They said it all so enthusiastically!
I just want to live a carefree life, and seriously, don’t put such heavy expectations on a high schooler! Besides, your daughter is an idol!
“Haah… I can’t rely on the parents anymore…”

Too many things to criticize, and realizing the outer defenses were completely sealed off gave me a headache. But even putting that aside, the immediate problem was being confined by those two during summer vacation.
During summer, the ‘Damenzu’ activities should be in full swing, but judging by how they are, they’ll probably take turns scheduling work so they can constantly watch me.
Worst case, they might create a fait accompli.
“I hate being confined… I just want to live carefree… I don’t want to be confined…”
I wanted to escape if possible, but the allowance they gave me had already become indispensable, so I couldn’t.
They had to keep being idols to support me financially.
For that to happen, I absolutely couldn’t cause any trouble. If it was just a scandal, I could probably have Ijuuin cover it up, but pregnancy was no joke.
I had to avoid confinement at all costs. For that, I needed allies.
With that resolve in my heart, I immediately pictured people who might become my allies.
It was a battle to see how many people I could bring over in just over two months.
I needed strong allies who could stand up to Setsuna and Arisa.

“Ichinose will probably listen to me, but Ijuuin is a no-go… Yuki-chan isn’t very reliable, but she’s a teacher, so she’s a candidate. Nekomiya hates me, so no way…? Well, she’s sensible, so maybe I can use Arisa as bait to get her to cooperate, then force my way in later… I’ll put that on hold for now… hmm…”
I kept listing and evaluating candidates, but no good results came to mind.
(Just the school members won’t cut it… If there was someone who knew the ‘Damenzu’ activities in detail and could interfere with their schedule, that would make things much easier…)
Only the other ‘Damenzu’ members or some bigwig at the agency could do that.
I knew the faces of the other two ‘Damenzu’ members from live videos, but I had no connection with them.
I knew they went to the same school, but there was never a chance to talk.
I briefly thought about having Setsuna and Arisa introduce me, but the timing was bad. They’d be wary, thinking I was going after another girl. And they wouldn’t be wrong.
More importantly, my bad reputation apparently extended to other grades, so even if I went to meet them, their classmates or friends would block me, making it a wasted effort.
So I gave up on contacting the ‘Damenzu’ members, but after running simulations in my head, only bad outcomes kept appearing and disappearing.
“Ah, screw it! I’m done thinking!”
I couldn’t help but shout, then leaned back on the bench and stared at the sky.
Maybe because I’d been using my brain, everything just felt troublesome.

“Ah, I wish someone would support me. Someone who just gives me money without complaining, always helps me when I’m in trouble, cheerfully takes care of all the hassles, and on top of that, doesn’t nag and just soothes me… I wonder if there’s someone like that out there…”
I gave up on thinking and let my desires spill out, but that kind of girl was probably too good to be true.
Still, I wanted one. I wonder if she’s somewhere out there. A goddess-like girl who wouldn’t turn yandere or try to confine me, just perfectly convenient for me alone…
“Onii-san. What are you doing?”
That was when I was thinking that.
“Hm? Who’s there?”
Suddenly, a voice came from nearby.
I quickly turned my face forward and saw a girl standing in front of the bench where I was sitting.
She wore a black baseball cap pulled low and a black mask covering half her face, but judging by her voice and the skirt she wore, there was no doubt who she was.
I glanced around quickly, but no one else was nearby. So she must be talking to me.
“Onii-san, do you mean me?”
“Yes. I was wondering what you were doing, looking up at the sky alone. I couldn’t help but get curious and talk to you. Was I bothering you?”
“No, not at all…”
When I answered, for some reason the girl in front of me seemed pleased.
(Huh? That voice sounds familiar somehow…)
Something about it nagged at me, but with the mask covering her face, I couldn’t confidently recall from memory. Same with her face.
Still, it was awkward to ask, “Hey, haven’t we met somewhere before?” in this situation. That would be outright hitting on her, and I had no intention of doing that.
(Well, whatever. I’m tired of thinking right now, so no need to force myself to remember.)
At least she didn’t seem to have a bad impression of me, so I decided to let it slide.
I didn’t want any unnecessary trouble anymore.
“You look pretty happy. What’s so good?”
“Onii-san, you have a face that Ruri really likes. It’s better to make a good impression than to be disliked, right? Besides…”
She kept her hands in the pockets of the black varsity jacket she wore over a white hoodie, narrowed her eyes, and leaned in closer.
“Hmmm, definitely Ruri’s type. That little bit of cloudiness in your eyes makes it even better. I might be seeing someone like this for the first time…”
Whether she was complimenting me or not was hard to tell, but her eyes sparkled with some kind of excitement. Still, her face was close. The brim of her hat almost touched my head.
“Hey, your face is too close. Step back a bit.”
“Oh, sorry.”
When I made a gesture to push her away, she immediately stepped back.
I thought she might be surprisingly straightforward, but she looked impressed for some reason.
“But wow… you’re not fazed at all. With such a cute girl right next to you, I’d think you’d be a little shy. Are you used to hanging out with girls?”
“Not really. I’m just used to seeing cute girls. Besides, I don’t judge girls by their looks.”
“Hmmm, is that so? Then what do you judge them by? Can you tell me?”
She leaned in again, but her eyes shone brightly, filled with undeniable curiosity.
“What the hell are you? You’re getting way too close for a first meeting.”
“Sorry. People have said that since I was little. Ruri is very curious and tends to put all her energy into what interests her. Right now, Ruri is very interested in you.”
“Interested?”
“Yes. Your face is exactly my type, but more than anything, I like interesting people. People who don’t bore me. If someone looks good but is boring, I lose interest. That’s just how Ruri is.”
I don’t care about that. Lately, I feel like I’m getting tangled up with troublesome people.
“Hmmm. So, if I answer, will you leave?”
“Yes. It all depends on your answer.”
She nodded, but it sounded awfully one-sided.
Well, whatever. If all I have to do is answer, I’ll do it.
Looking into the excited girl’s eyes, I slowly opened my mouth.
“Money.”
“Huh?”
“I said, money. How much money you have and how much you’ll spend on me is my standard for judging girls.”
“Eh? M-money? You mean you’re after money?”
“To put it bluntly, yes.”
For some reason, people are usually surprised when I say I like money. Everyone likes money, so I don’t get what’s so strange.
But I’m used to it now, so whatever.
“B-but, you’re a high schooler, right? Normally, high schoolers focus more on cuteness or figure…”
“I don’t care about looks or body. I just want a girl who has enough money to support me and let me play for life. Anyone, any number of girls, all welcome. That’s my answer.”
The girl lowered her head and fell silent. Maybe she was as exasperated as Nekomiya.
If that’s the case, fine. I don’t intend to get involved, so I don’t care.
“Are you satisfied now? If you’re done, then get lost. I’ve got too many worries and I’m tired.”
I said that and looked up at the sky for the third time.
As always, the blue sky was cloudless.
Looking at it doesn’t make my tiny worries disappear, but somehow it does make me feel a little better.
I hope the clear May sky and breeze bring some placebo effect, but I’m not counting on it.
If anything, I might feel grateful if this girl just leaves quickly.
That’s what I was thinking when suddenly—
“Puh, ku, kukuku…”
What I heard wasn’t footsteps fading away.
It sounded like someone was trying to hold back laughter, so I looked over and saw the girl holding her stomach, looking down.
“Ahaha, ahahaha! O-onii-san! You’re hilarious! I never expected that! Saying you want money right to my face!? You’re such a scumbag! You’re the best, onii-san!”
She burst out laughing, but I didn’t know how to react.
“Is it really that funny? I wasn’t trying to be funny; that’s my honest opinion.”

“If you’re serious, that’s even worse! Saying that to a cute girl like me! No way, I’ve never met someone who fits my type so perfectly! Seriously, you’re such a scumbag, onii-san! I was just killing time before my lesson, but meeting someone like you means I’m lucky! You’re seriously the worst!”
“You say scumbag way too much…”
What a rude girl. I was tired and couldn’t deal with her anymore.
“That’s enough. I’m heading home first. Later, unknown laughing girl. We probably won’t meet again, but take care.”
“Ah, wait a minute!”
I stood up from the bench and tried to go home, but for some reason, she stopped me.
“What now? You still got something to say?”
“Yes. Ruri is really interested in you, scumbag onii-san. I’ve never met someone this interesting before. I absolutely don’t want this to be the last time.”
“Eh… even if you say that… did you hear what I said earlier? I’m not interested in people without money.”
Especially not troublesome ones.
But before I could say that, the girl said,
“Ruri has money.”
“I kind of suspected it, but you really didn’t notice, huh? It’s a bit disappointing, but oh well.”
She looked a little dissatisfied as she took off her hat.
Suddenly, her hidden red hair softly fell onto her shoulder.
“Because Ruri is going to shine even more and become popular. I plan to snatch the center position soon. The true ace of ‘Dimension Stars!’ is this Ruri!”
Then she touched the black mask with her finger.
As her slender fingertip pulled it down, her hidden face was revealed, and I couldn’t help but open my eyes wide.
“You’re…!”
“Finally, you recognized me. Yes, I’m Ruri Tachibana, the next ace and future top idol of ‘Dimension Stars!’”
There stood Ruri, a member of ‘Dimension Stars!’ alongside Setsuna and Arisa.
I couldn’t hide my surprise at this unexpected encounter.
“Ruri and scumbag onii-san are going to have a long relationship, so from now on, please remember Ruri well, scumbag onii-san.”
“A long relationship…?”
“Yes. Ruri really likes you, scumbag onii-san. So Ruri will become a girl who is convenient for you. A special service just for fans, kept secret.”
Still not fully grasping the situation, I saw Ruri flash a bewitching smile and say,
“I’ll take the top idol spot and onii-san too! Ruri will support you, scumbag onii-san♪”
And with that, she smiled like a little devil.
